# Learning and Mastering Redis with C++ and Hiredis

## Course Overview

This course combines **in-memory data structure mastery** with **practical Redis integration** using C++, positioning you as a specialist in high-performance system design. Redis is a critical component in modern backend architectures—used for caching, real-time analytics, message queues, and distributed locks. By learning Redis fundamentals alongside the Hiredis C client library, you'll understand both the **theoretical DSA principles** and **real-world implementation patterns**.

**Who it's for:**
- Backend engineers preparing for systems design interviews
- Competitive programmers wanting practical distributed systems experience
- Developers building high-throughput applications
- Candidates targeting FAANG or fintech roles

**Why it matters for interview prep:**
- Redis questions appear in system design rounds (caching strategies, rate limiting, leaderboards)
- Demonstrates understanding of trade-offs between memory, speed, and durability
- Shows proficiency with non-relational databases and NoSQL patterns
- Practical coding exercises prepare you for real implementation scenarios

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **Redis Data Structures & Operations** – Strings, Lists, Sets, Sorted Sets, Hashes, Streams; O(n) complexity analysis for each
- **Hiredis Client Library** – Connection pooling, pipelining, pub/sub patterns, error handling in C++
- **Cache Design Patterns** – LRU/LFU eviction, cache-aside, write-through, distributed caching strategies
- **Key-Value Algorithm Problems** – Counting, frequency tables, sliding windows, range queries using Redis primitives
- **Transactions & Atomicity** – MULTI/EXEC, Lua scripting, optimistic locking with WATCH
- **Persistence & Replication** – RDB snapshots, AOF logs, master-slave architecture, data durability guarantees
- **Performance Optimization** – Connection pooling, batch operations, memory profiling, latency analysis
- **Real-World System Patterns** – Rate limiting (token bucket), leaderboards, session storage, real-time counters

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### **Phase 1: Redis Fundamentals & Data Structures (Tasks 1–25)**

**Week 1-2: Core Concepts**
1. Install Redis server and understand the event loop model
2. Master 5 basic data structures: STRING, LIST, SET, ZSET, HASH
3. Understand key expiration, TTL, and memory management
4. Learn O(n) complexity for each operation type
5. Practice basic CRUD operations via redis-cli

**Week 3: Hiredis Integration (Tasks 6–15)**
6. Set up Hiredis C library with C++ wrapper classes
7. Establish connection pooling pattern
8. Implement error handling and timeout logic
9. Build a simple key-value store client
10. Practice string and list operations programmatically

**Week 4: Algorithm Foundations (Tasks 16–25)**
11. Implement frequency counters using HSET/HGET
12. Solve sliding window problems with LPUSH/RPOP
13. Build a leaderboard with ZADD/ZRANGE
14. Implement unique visitor tracking with SET operations
15. Design and code a basic LRU cache using ZSET timestamps

---

### **Phase 2: Intermediate Patterns & DSA (Tasks 26–60)**

**Week 5-6: Caching & Eviction Strategies**
16. Implement cache-aside pattern (check cache, miss→DB, update cache)
17. Build LRU eviction using Lua scripting with ZSET
18. Design write-through cache with consistency
19. Implement distributed caching with key versioning
20. Solve "Design a Cache" interview problems

**Tasks 20–35: String & Hash-Based Problems**
21. Count word frequency in documents (HINCRBY)
22. Implement autocomplete prefix search with Sorted Sets
23. Build a session store with HSET field-level expiration
24. Solve "Two Sum" variant using HSET lookups
25. Implement rate limiter with sliding window counters

**Tasks 36–50: List & Queue Operations**
26. Build a task queue with LPUSH/RPOP pattern
27. Implement a message broker with pub/sub
28. Design a job scheduling system (delayed tasks)
29. Solve "Median of Data Stream" using two sorted sets
30. Implement circular buffer pattern with LRANGE

**Tasks 51–60: Set & Sorted Set Mastery**
31. Find intersection/union of user groups (SINTER/SUNION)
32. Build a social recommendation engine
33. Implement range queries with ZRANGEBYSCORE
34. Design a time-series data structure for analytics
35. Solve "Top K Elements" with ZSET operations

---

### **Phase 3: Advanced Patterns & System Design (Tasks 61–98)**

**Week 7-8: Transactions & Atomicity (Tasks 36–50)**
36. Implement WATCH/MULTI/EXEC optimistic locking
37. Build a distributed counter with Lua atomicity
38. Design a transfer system (debit/credit with rollback)
39. Implement compare-and-swap patterns
40. Solve "Stock Trading with Transaction Handling"

**Week 9: Persistence & Replication (Tasks 51–70)**
41. Configure RDB snapshots and understand trade-offs
42. Implement AOF persistence for durability
43. Design master-slave replication monitoring
44. Build failover detection and recovery
45. Understand consistency models (eventual vs. strong)

**Week 10: Stream & Pub/Sub Patterns (Tasks 71–80)**
46. Implement Redis Streams for event sourcing
47. Build a real-time notification system
48. Design a consumer group for parallel processing
49. Implement backpressure handling in pub/sub
50. Solve "Message Queue with Ordering" pattern

**Week 11: System Design Integration (Tasks 81–98)**
51. Design a distributed rate limiter (token bucket)
52. Build a leaderboard with real-time updates
53. Implement a distributed lock (Redlock algorithm)
54. Design a session store for multi-server deployment
55. Build a bloom filter for duplicate detection
56. Implement a full-text search index cache layer
57. Design a real-time analytics dashboard cache
58. Build a circuit breaker pattern with Redis health checks

---

## Key Skills You'll Build

### **Data Structure Mastery**
- Choosing the right Redis type for each problem (String vs. List vs. Set vs. Sorted Set)
- Understanding time complexity trade-offs and optimization opportunities
- Designing composite structures (combining hashes with sets/sorted sets)

### **C++ Integration & Hiredis**
```cpp
// Skill: Connection pooling and command batching
class RedisClient {
    redisContext* ctx;
    
public:
    void batchIncrement(const std::vector<std::string>& keys) {
        for (const auto& key : keys) {
            redisAppendCommand(ctx, "INCR %s", key.c_str());
        }
        // Single roundtrip for multiple commands
        for (size_t i = 0; i < keys.size(); i++) {
            redisReply* reply = redisGetReply(ctx, nullptr);
            freeReplyObject(reply);
        }
    }
};
```

### **Algorithm Problem Solving**
- Converting interview problems into Redis operations
- Optimizing for latency and throughput
- Handling edge cases with Lua scripting

### **System Design Thinking**
- Cache invalidation strategies
- Distributed coordination patterns
- Handling failures and eventual consistency
- Performance monitoring and optimization

### **Code Quality & Production Readiness**
- Error handling and reconnection logic
- Memory leak prevention with proper cleanup
- Connection pooling and resource management
- Thread-safe Redis client design

---
